deities: Mata Murti - mother of the twin sages Nar and Narayan (an incarnation of Lord Vishnu); the family deity of the Garhwal region
festivals: Mata Murti Ka Mela (Shravan Dwadashi / Vaman Dwadashi, Bhadrapada month, August-September; Mahabhishek, Geeta Path, Bhagavat Pooja in the mornings, Geet Govinda recital and Aarti in the evenings, with Vedic Ashtotram and Sahasranama recitations)

history.dynasty: Not documented (small shrine; no dynasty attribution found)
history.summary: Identity confirmed: the small Mata Murti temple ~3 km from the Badrinath shrine on the right bank of the Alaknanda, reached by a short easy trek (30 min-1 hr) on the Mana route. It is dedicated to Mata Murti, mother of the twins Nar and Narayan, who are an incarnation of Lord Vishnu: legend says her deep penance persuaded Vishnu to take birth from her womb as the twins to slay a demon; praying here is believed to free one from worldly suffering. The annual Mata Murti fair (August-September) honours her and commemorates the descent of the Ganges on earth. name: Mata Murti Temple

town_description: The Mata Murti shrine lies a short trek from Badrinath town on the right bank of the Alaknanda, on the way toward Mana, the last village on the Indo-Tibet border. Badrinath itself is the Char Dham temple town in Chamoli district at 3,133 m.
